title: Two Motions Pull the Sisters Apart

scenes.tts: In chapter one, separase cut the cohesin links, and the sisters began to part. But what carries them apart? Two things move at once.
scenes.visual: THE ONE WORLD from chapter 1, picked up where it ended: the grey cell oval fills the frame, yellow poles at far left and far right, grey spindle fibres between them. At the middle, THE HERO pair (blue sister rods, orange kinetochore dots) with two teal chips labelled 'cohesin' split into fragments and drifting off its centromere; the green separase shape fades away. The two blue sisters start to slide apart. On 'what carries them apart?' the question appears as large text over the upper frame. On 'Two things move', BOTH the sisters and the yellow poles begin to move outward together, so the viewer sees two motions at once.
scenes.narration: In chapter one, separase cut the cohesin links, and the sisters began to part. But what carries them apart? Two things move at once.

scenes.visual: Title 'Two Motions Pull the Sisters Apart' over the same world; the sisters and poles keep drifting outward slowly.

scenes.tts: Watch two distances. In anaphase A, each sister moves toward its pole. In anaphase B, the poles themselves move apart. The first changes chromosome-to-pole distance. The second changes pole-to-pole distance.
scenes.visual: Show then tell. Rewind the hero to anaphase onset. Two orange brackets appear, each from one orange kinetochore to its own yellow pole; as the sisters move, both orange brackets shrink, label 'anaphase A' (orange). Then a long yellow bracket spans pole to pole above the cell and grows as the poles slide outward, label 'anaphase B' (yellow). Brackets are schematic; no numbers yet.
scenes.narration: Watch two distances. In anaphase A, each sister moves toward its pole. In anaphase B, the poles themselves move apart. The first changes chromosome-to-pole distance. The second changes pole-to-pole distance.

scenes.tts: In anaphase A, each kay fibre, the bundle from a kinetochore to its pole, gets shorter. A kay fibre contains many microtubules, not one rope. But where does it lose its subunits?
scenes.caption: In anaphase A, each k-fibre, the bundle from a kinetochore to its pole, gets shorter. A k-fibre contains many microtubules, not one rope. But where does it lose its subunits?
scenes.visual: Camera eases in on the left half: one orange kinetochore and its grey k-fibre running to the left yellow pole, filling about 60% of frame height. The fibre is drawn as a bundle of 4 parallel grey lines, label 'k-fibre' (TEXT). As the kinetochore creeps toward the pole the fibre visibly shortens. Two small question marks pulse, one at the kinetochore end and one at the pole end.
scenes.narration: In anaphase A, each k-fibre, the bundle from a kinetochore to its pole, gets shorter. A k-fibre contains many microtubules, not one rope. But where does it lose its subunits?

scenes.tts: In 1988, Gorbsky, Sammak and Borisy made the fibres glow in cultured mammalian cells. Then they bleached a dark stripe across the anaphase spindle. They tracked poles, chromosomes, and the stripe in living cells.
scenes.visual: The grey fibres turn bright white-green (glowing, label 'fluorescent tubulin'). A thin white laser line sweeps vertically across the spindle halfway between the kinetochore and the pole; where it passes, the glowing fibres go dark, leaving a dark band across them, label 'bleached stripe' (TEXT). Label at bottom: 'cultured mammalian cells, 1988' (TEXT).
scenes.narration: In 1988, Gorbsky, Sammak and Borisy made the fibres glow in cultured mammalian cells. Then they bleached a dark stripe across the anaphase spindle. They tracked poles, chromosomes, and the stripe in living cells.

scenes.tts: If the pole reeled the fibres in, the stripe would ride toward the pole with the chromosome. So which way does the stripe go?
scenes.visual: A ghost preview at 50% opacity shows the reel-in idea: the fibre slides into the pole like rope into a winch, carrying the dark stripe poleward alongside the chromosome; small winch icon at the pole, label 'reeled in at pole?' (TEXT). The ghost fades back to the real fibre with its stripe. Question text 'Which way does the stripe go?' appears large.
scenes.narration: If the pole reeled the fibres in, the stripe would ride toward the pole with the chromosome. So which way does the stripe go?

scenes.visual: Thinking pause. Question 'Which way does the stripe go?' stays on screen. Freeze the experimental movie and show a small pause icon, so the stripe's outcome is not revealed during the prediction. Only the question text breathes gently.

scenes.tts: The stripe did not move detectably relative to the near pole. The chromosome moved toward it, shortening the fibre between kinetochore and stripe. So these fibres lost subunits mainly at the kinetochore.
scenes.visual: Question and pause icon fade. The dark stripe stays fixed relative to the near yellow pole as both can move with anaphase B; the orange kinetochore and its blue sister slide toward the stripe. The glowing stretch between kinetochore and stripe gets shorter; the stretch between stripe and near pole stays the same length (small grey ruler ticks show it unchanged, schematic). Tiny grey subunit dots fall off the fibre at the kinetochore end, label 'lost at kinetochore' (orange).
scenes.narration: The stripe did not move detectably relative to the near pole. The chromosome moved toward it, shortening the fibre between kinetochore and stripe. So these fibres lost subunits mainly at the kinetochore.

scenes.tts: A small loss elsewhere was not ruled out. Poleward flux means the microtubule lattice itself moves toward the pole. In fruit-fly embryos and frog egg-extract spindles, flux can contribute much more.
scenes.visual: Keep the carried fibre. A faint second trickle of grey dots appears at the pole end, label 'small loss here not excluded' (TEXT). Then transform that same fibre into a contrasting schematic labelled 'fruit-fly embryo / frog egg extract': the bleached stripe and lattice slide toward the pole while dots fall off near the pole, label 'poleward lattice flux' (yellow). Mark the view 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: A small loss elsewhere was not ruled out. Poleward flux means the microtubule lattice itself moves toward the pole. In fruit-fly embryos and frog egg-extract spindles, flux can contribute much more.

scenes.tts: Anaphase B has its own engines. In many animal cells, motors slide overlapping midzone fibres apart. Dynein at the cell cortex, its edge, pulls on astral fibres. Their balance differs among cell types.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls back to the full cell. In the middle, fibres from the two poles overlap; small purple motor blobs walk on the overlap and push the two sets apart, label 'midzone motors' (purple). Short astral fibres fan from each yellow pole to the cell edge; small green dynein blobs at the grey outline tug them outward, label 'cortical dynein' (green). The yellow pole-to-pole bracket grows as both act.
scenes.narration: Anaphase B has its own engines. In many animal cells, motors slide overlapping midzone fibres apart. Dynein at the cell cortex, its edge, pulls on astral fibres. Their balance differs among cell types.

scenes.tts: Now read a movie, with example numbers. Each kinetochore closes on its pole at one micrometre a minute. The poles separate at one micrometre a minute. These are illustrative, not a universal speed.
scenes.caption: Now read a movie, with example numbers. Each kinetochore closes on its pole at 1 µm a minute. The poles separate at 1 µm a minute. These are illustrative, not a universal speed.
scenes.visual: A computed position-versus-time plot slides in below the cell (x: time 0 to 4 min; y: position along the spindle, um), label 'illustrative numbers'. Four lines are drawn live as the cell animates: the two yellow pole lines start at plus and minus 6 um and move to plus and minus 8; the two orange kinetochore lines start at plus and minus 0.5 and move to plus and minus 6.5. Rate tags pop on: 'anaphase A: 1.0 µm/min' (orange) beside one kinetochore-to-pole gap, 'anaphase B: 1.0 µm/min' (yellow) beside the pole-to-pole gap.
scenes.narration: Now read a movie, with example numbers. Each kinetochore closes on its pole at 1 µm a minute. The poles separate at 1 µm a minute. These are illustrative, not a universal speed.

scenes.tts: So how fast do the sisters separate? Each closes on its own pole while the poles move apart. Two times one, plus one: three micrometres a minute. In this symmetric movie, sister separation is twice A plus B.
scenes.caption: So how fast do the sisters separate? Each closes on its own pole while the poles move apart. 2 × 1, plus 1: 3 µm a minute. In this symmetric movie, sister separation is twice A plus B.
scenes.visual: On the computed plot, a blue band fills the gap between the two orange kinetochore lines and widens from 1 um to 13 um over 4 min, label 'sister separation' (blue). The sum builds as stacked blocks beside it: two orange blocks 'A' plus one yellow block 'B' slide together into one blue block '3.0 µm/min'.
scenes.narration: So how fast do the sisters separate? Each closes on its own pole while the poles move apart. 2 × 1, plus 1: 3 µm a minute. In this symmetric movie, sister separation is twice A plus B.

scenes.tts: Hide the poles. A movie tracking only chromosomes sees that three, but cannot tell how much came from the poles. Without that landmark, A and B are indistinguishable.
scenes.visual: The two yellow pole lines on the plot and the yellow poles in the cell fade to dotted outlines; the blue band stays. The orange and yellow blocks under the blue '3.0' block blur together into a grey question mark, label 'A or B?' (TEXT).
scenes.narration: Hide the poles. A movie tracking only chromosomes sees that three, but cannot tell how much came from the poles. Without that landmark, A and B are indistinguishable.

scenes.tts: The two motions add: chromosomes travel along shortening fibres while the poles spread apart. Measure each against its own landmark. Those landmarks keep the rates from being confused. Sisters part by two motions: chromosomes to poles, poles apart.
scenes.visual: The poles return solid. Full anaphase plays once more in the same world: orange brackets shrink, the yellow bracket grows, and the blue sister gap widens. The orange, yellow and blue labels glow in turn as each narrated motion is named. End on the two changing brackets and the widening sister gap.
scenes.narration: The two motions add: chromosomes travel along shortening fibres while the poles spread apart. Measure each against its own landmark. Those landmarks keep the rates from being confused. Sisters part by two motions: chromosomes to poles, poles apart.

scenes.line: Sisters part by two motions: chromosomes to poles, poles apart.
